# The US veto on the record - which bills each president vetoed, each candidate rule's base and precision, and what a party-bloc Congress could send (R-US17)

Read on `ElectionsData/usa/us_veto_measures.csv` (`Tools/us_veto_prep.pl`: every public law and every vetoed measure of the 115th-119th Congresses decided from noon on 20 January 2017, each chamber's final agreement and its party split from the Clerk's and the Senate's roll calls; the record is `ElectionsData/usa/veto_record.md`). A rule reads the chamber's final agreement; one with no roll call (voice vote, unanimous consent) names nothing. VETOED: vetoed, pocket vetoed, or vetoed and overridden.

## The party-bloc Congress under Rule XXII

**The plan's premise - each party one stance, in both chambers** (spec-risk 4, "each party voting as one"): a measure the president's party opposes reaches him only if the other party carries both chambers alone. The seats, each Congress's last roll call's:

| Congress | House R - D (sworn) | Senate R - D, independents in their caucus (sworn) |
|---|---|---|
| 115th | 235 - 197 (432) | 51 - 49 (100) |
| 116th | 195 - 232 (429) | 52 - 48 (100) |
| 117th | 213 - 218 (431) | 50 - 50 (100) |
| 118th | 219 - 211 (430) | 49 - 51 (100) |
| 119th | 218 - 214 (433) | 53 - 47 (100) |

- Of the 34 measures the president's party opposed in a chamber (F3's count), a one-stance bloc Congress sends **0** (Donald J. Trump (first term) 0, Joseph R. Biden Jr. 0, Donald J. Trump (second term) 0).

**Chamber by chamber, as recorded** (each chamber's blocs voting as their members voted there - a party may stand one way in the House and another in the Senate; the reading this document declared before its first run):

- Of the record's 25 vetoed measures, it could have sent **5** to the president.
- Of all 1564 measures decided, it sends 1512; of those, **13** are VETOABLE - the president's party bloc opposed in a chamber (Donald J. Trump (first term) 9, Joseph R. Biden Jr. 4, Donald J. Trump (second term) 0).

## The verdict (R-US17)

B1's precision on Poland's whole term, recomputed from the Sejm's CSV: **45 of 166 (27.1 %)**. "Far more" (declared before the first run, PROVISIONAL): a rule whose pooled precision is below it.

**STOPPED - R-US17 is re-asked:** a party-bloc Congress under Rule XXII never sends a vetoable measure under the plan's premise, each party one stance in both chambers (0 of 34 opposed; chamber by chamber, as recorded, it sends 13). On the matrix alone (a) would be recommended: its pooled precision 66.7 % is at least B1's 27.1 %.

The rules below B1's precision: none.
